questions.question: Which sequence shows the accounting cycle in the correct order?
options: Source documents, journals, ledger, trial balance, final accounts, financial statements
Journals, source documents, trial balance, ledger, financial statements, final accounts
Source documents, ledger, journals, final accounts, trial balance, financial statements
Trial balance, journals, source documents, ledger, financial statements, final accounts

questions.question: Why is the process called a 'cycle' rather than a straight line?
options: Because the trial balance is checked twice
Because the same sequence repeats for every new accounting period
Because debits and credits circle between accounts
Because the owner reviews the books in rotation

questions.question: The two key questions the accounting cycle ultimately answers for a sole trader are:
options: How many transactions occurred, and who recorded them
Which journal is largest, and which account has the most entries
Did the business make a profit, and what is its financial position
How much tax is owed, and how many debtors exist

subtopics.title: Stage One and Two — Source Documents and Journals

questions.question: Mokoena Traders sells goods for cash on 3 June. Which source document is produced, and into which journal is it entered?
options: An invoice, entered in the Creditors Journal
A cash register slip, entered in the Cash Receipts Journal
A receipt, entered in the Cash Payments Journal
A cash register slip, entered in the Petty Cash Journal

questions.question: What is the main reason transactions are first sorted into journals instead of being entered straight into the ledger?
options: The ledger is only opened at year end
Journals calculate profit automatically
Similar transactions are grouped so only column totals need to be posted
Source documents cannot be read by the bookkeeper

questions.question: What does the source-document stage produce for the cycle?
options: The evidence proving the date, amount and parties of each transaction
The balance of every ledger account
The gross profit for the year
A chronological list of posted totals

questions.question: Wages are paid by electronic transfer. In which journal does this entry belong?
options: Cash Receipts Journal
Debtors Journal
Petty Cash Journal
Cash Payments Journal

subtopics.title: Stage Three and Four — Posting to the Ledger and the Trial Balance

questions.question: When the CRJ bank column total is posted at month end, the double entry is:
options: Debit Sales, credit Bank
Debit Bank, credit Sales
Debit Bank, credit Capital
Debit Trading account, credit Bank

questions.question: The journals are organised by date. How is the general ledger organised?
options: By account, gathering all entries that affect one item
By source document number
By the size of each transaction
By the name of the bookkeeper who posted it

questions.question: A trial balance balances, but R500 paid for Telephone was posted to the debit of Repairs. What does this show?
options: The trial balance will not balance until the error is fixed
A balancing trial balance proves the ledger is completely correct
The trial balance checks arithmetic equality, not perfect accuracy
The error will be corrected automatically in the final accounts

subtopics.title: Stage Five and Six — Final Accounts and Financial Statements

questions.question: In the final accounts, gross profit is calculated in the Trading account and then transferred to:
options: The Bank account
The Profit and Loss account
The Capital account directly
The trial balance

questions.question: Why is net profit transferred to the Capital account?
options: Because profit must be kept away from the owner
Because the bank requires it
Because the profit belongs to the owner and increases owner's equity
Because expenses are recorded there

questions.question: Which statement reports the assets, equity and liabilities of the business on the last day of the period?
options: The Statement of Comprehensive Income
The trial balance
The Trading account
The Statement of Financial Position

questions.question: A cash sale's till slip amount eventually reaches the financial statements. Which route does it travel?
options: CRJ, then ledger, then trial balance, then final accounts, then statements
Ledger, then CRJ, then final accounts, then trial balance, then statements
Trial balance, then CRJ, then ledger, then statements, then final accounts
CRJ, then trial balance, then ledger, then statements, then final accounts
